title.en: History: Social and Religious Reform Movements in the 19th Century

text.en: Meena learnt about a reformer who ended a cruel custom in India. "Raja Ram Mohan Roy," said her teacher.

In the nineteenth century, social and religious reformers worked to end evil customs. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj and fought sati, which was banned in 1829. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked for widow remarriage.
Dayananda Saraswati started the Arya Samaj and Ramakrishna and Vivekananda spread the message of service. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan promoted modern education among Muslims at Aligarh. Jyotiba Phule fought caste discrimination.
In Tamil Nadu, Vallalar Ramalinga Adigal taught compassion, Iyothee Thass worked for the oppressed, and Muthulakshmi Reddy and others worked for women. The reforms led to laws and a new social awakening.
